questions.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].

$$

$$
{U}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}5\end{aligned}],\,{V}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
{V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}_{r}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of ${Σ}_{r}.$

First, notice that

$$
{Σ}_{r}^{+}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}],\,{U}_{r}^{T}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{U}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{aligned}],\,{V}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
{V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}_{r}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of ${Σ}_{r}.$

First, notice that

$$
{V}_{r}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}=\frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{U}_{r}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & -5 \\ 10 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
